newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up slightly on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up slightly on foreign buying.

text.p: Despite several bouts of profit-taking, Thai stocks closed slightly higher on Wednesday as foreigners bought some large capitalised banking, finance and energy issues late, brokers said.

"The market was not bullish as it lacked positive news to boost investment. Investors preferred to stay on the sidelines awaiting release of first quarter earnings of finance companies due later this month," said Somchai Trairattanapirom of SITCA Investment and Securities.
The composite SET index ended up 3.27 points to 716.89 on 2.8 billion baht turnover.
The SET-50 index gained 0.45 point to 53.98.
Advancers edged decliners 129 to 118 while 106 issues were unchanged.
Brokers said the market was also sluggish because many traders had not yet returned from the Thai traditional New Year holidays which began last Saturday and ended on Tuesday.
Somchai said short-term investors bought some banking stocks in the morning but sold them later on, making the index to move a bit erratically during the afternoon session.
Medium-sized Bank of Ayudhya Plc gained two baht to 73 despite a Standard & Poor's decision to cut the bank's short-term counterparty rating to "A3" from "A2" earlier on Wednesday.
The banking sector rose most in terms of value, rising 0.37 percent, followed by the communication sector advancing 1.40 percent.
Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, unchanged at 125 baht. TelecomAsia gained one to 47.75 and Delta Electronics shed eight to 78.
